title: Gemcitabine and cisplatin induction before chemoradiotherapy
indication_text: Induction chemotherapy before concurrent chemoradiotherapy for locally advanced nasopharyngeal cancer.
purpose: This chemotherapy is given before chemoradiotherapy to improve cancer control. Induction is the first stage of the planned pathway, and does not replace the later treatment.
schedule_label: Day 1: both drugs; Day 8: gemcitabine. Every 21 days, up to 3 cycles.
schedule_summary: Gemcitabine 1,000 mg/m² on Days 1 and 8, with cisplatin 80 mg/m² on Day 1, every 21 days for a maximum of 3 cycles.
administration_text: Gemcitabine runs over 30 minutes, followed on Day 1 by cisplatin over 1 hour. Prescribed fluids before and after cisplatin lengthen the visit. Day 8 is gemcitabine alone.
monitoring_summary: Day 1: full blood count, kidney and liver tests. Day 8: full blood count. Audiology is arranged when clinically indicated; extra tests depend on symptoms and results.

agents.name: Gemcitabine
agents.explanation: Gemcitabine is converted inside cells into forms that disrupt DNA building blocks and DNA copying. It can affect normal blood-cell production as well as cancer cells.
agents.watch: Report fever, unusual bruising, breathlessness, swelling or reduced urine urgently. Flu-like symptoms cannot safely be assumed to be a harmless drug effect.
risks: Low blood counts, infection and bleeding
Flu-like symptoms, fatigue, rash and swelling
Uncommon serious lung or liver injury
Rare haemolytic uraemic syndrome and kidney injury
Effects on fertility; pregnancy and breastfeeding need specialist advice

agents.name: Cisplatin
agents.explanation: Cisplatin links strands of DNA, the instructions inside cells, making it harder for cancer cells to repair damage and divide. Healthy cells may also be affected. Kidney function, hearing, blood counts and nerve symptoms help the team decide whether the next dose is safe.
agents.watch: Report reduced urine, persistent vomiting, tinnitus, hearing change or new tingling.
risks: Low blood counts and serious infection
Hearing loss or tinnitus, which can persist
Infusion reaction and effects on fertility

anatomy: Tiredness can affect activity and concentration. Balance activity and rest; report sudden confusion.
Report soreness, ulcers or difficulty swallowing. Ask early about mouth care, pain relief and nutrition.
New or worsening breathlessness, cough or chest symptoms need urgent advice; lung inflammation can be serious.
Fever, shivering, sudden illness, unexplained bruising or bleeding needs urgent oncology advice.
Take prescribed anti-sickness medicines. Report persistent vomiting, diarrhoea, dehydration or inability to drink.
Report reduced urine, swelling or poor fluid intake. Blood tests help detect kidney injury.
Report severe rash, blistering, facial swelling or breathing symptoms promptly. Tell staff about pain at the infusion site.
Discuss fertility preservation, contraception, pregnancy and breastfeeding before treatment.
Report ringing, hearing loss, numbness or tingling before the next dose; some effects can persist.

support.title: Preventing and treating sickness
support.text: Use the prescribed medicines for the active treatment day. The cisplatin combination visit has high sickness risk; Day 8 is gemcitabine alone and has a separate plan.

support.title: Fluids with cisplatin
support.text: Cisplatin needs prescribed fluids before and after treatment. Follow your individual drinking plan for the next 24 hours; heart or kidney conditions may change it. Call if vomiting prevents drinking or urine falls.

support.title: Mouth care and nutrition
support.text: Follow your unit’s oral-care plan. Tell the team early about mouth pain, weight loss, choking or difficulty eating and drinking. Dietetic and swallowing support can help.

support.title: Fever and sudden illness
support.text: Fever, shivering, sudden illness, unusual bleeding, new breathlessness, persistent vomiting or inability to drink needs urgent oncology advice. Severe chest pain, severe breathing difficulty, collapse or a seizure is an emergency: call 112/999.

support.title: Medicine review
support.text: Bring prescription, non-prescription and herbal medicines. Check interactions, allergies and any changes with the oncology pharmacist.

support.title: Recovery and practical support
support.text: Ask about fatigue, work, transport, caring responsibilities, emotional support and help with appointments.

evidence.title: Understanding the evidence
evidence.intro: The national regimen brings together research and specialist guidance for a specific treatment setting.
evidence.population: Induction chemotherapy before concurrent chemoradiotherapy for locally advanced nasopharyngeal cancer.
evidence.comparison: Discuss the alternatives appropriate to your cancer and health.
evidence.interpretation: A randomised study of 480 patients compared this three-cycle induction approach followed by chemoradiotherapy with chemoradiotherapy alone. At three years, 85.3% versus 76.5% were alive without recurrence. Severe acute side effects were more frequent with induction (75.7% versus 55.7%). These group results do not predict your personal outcome.
limitations: Different doses, disease settings and treatment sequences are not interchangeable.
Group study results cannot predict an individual outcome.
